The paper that matches this is Momentum-Coupled Rubric Adaptation for Detailed Image Captioning [1]. It improves picture descriptions by using one shared vision-language model for three roles: generating captions, generating detailed quality rubrics, and judging captions against those rubrics, instead of using separate models that may become inconsistent [1].

Its key idea is a momentum update: after the caption policy changes, the rubric generator and judge are updated through an exponential moving average of the policy parameters, using one shared momentum model [1]. The rubrics are created online from sampled captions, reference captions, and image evidence, and the judge uses them to give rubric-based rewards while only the caption policy is directly updated [1]. The paper reports strong gains on five captioning benchmarks, including the highest average score in caption-based question answering [1].
